explanation: The theorem says that for every unit d of ZMod M there is a matrix γ ∈ SL(2,ℤ) lying in Γ₀(M) (i.e. lower-left entry ≡ 0 mod M) whose top-left entry reduces to d — equivalently, surjectivity of the natural map Γ₀(M) → (ZMod M)ˣ on top-left/bottom-right entries. I searched Mathlib for this: `Gamma0`, `Gamma0Map` (only in Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups.lean, where `Gamma0Map : Γ₀ N →* ZMod N` is the bottom-right entry and there is no surjectivity result, only `Gamma1' = ker`), for surjectivity statements in Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms (only `surjective_cosetToCuspOrbit` for cusps), for a diamond operator / Hecke character (nothing in Mathlib), and for existence lemmas producing SL(2,·) matrices with prescribed entries (`IsCoprime.exists_SL2_row`, `IsCoprime.exists_SL2_col` in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialLinearGroup.lean). The latter give an SL(2,R) matrix with a prescribed row/column when the two entries are coprime in a commutative ring, but they say nothing about membership in Γ₀(M) or about a prescribed top-left entry with vanishing lower-left entry mod M; deriving the theorem from them would need a construction of the matrix and a couple of extra congruences, well beyond one or two lines of glue. The library's own proof instead uses its private Mathlib-free result `CohCarrier.gamma0Units_surjective` (Definitions/Def_CohCarrier_Inst.lean), which has no counterpart in Mathlib.
